channel.title: RAN Air Wing dev blog
channel.description: HMAS Melbourne (R21) flight sim: history, carrier operations and dev diary.

item.title: 26 November 1959: fixed-wing flying to end, then a reprieve
item.description: On this date in 1959 the Minister announced fixed-wing naval aviation would end in 1963.

item.title: Making the deck sound right
item.description: Gear, flaps, speedbrakes and hook each got their own sound instead of a generic click.

item.title: 1959: Hollywood comes aboard
item.description: A lighter post: the carrier takes a role in a feature film.

item.title: The home screen now cuts between launches, landings and the escorts
item.description: On the home screen the orbit camera now cuts between a chase view of each landing, a front view and orbit of each launch, patrol shots, and close-ups of the escort ships.

item.title: After a crash, the camera circles the wreck
item.description: When you crash, the sim now cuts to the chase view and slowly orbits the crash site instead of leaving you looking out of the cockpit.

item.title: The home screen now has a working flight deck
item.description: A Tracker and a Skyhawk now take turns launching, circling the carrier, recovering and parking on the home screen. The Tracker folds its wings. The lift routine and the helicopter are gone.

item.title: Name tags over the ships
item.description: HMAS Melbourne, Perth, Derwent and Supply now carry a name tag overhead, like Pedro the plane guard helicopter, so you can tell which ship is which from a distance.

item.title: Catapult launch, step by step
item.description: Six steps from the catapult to level flight at 1,000 ft, with the reasons behind each.

item.title: Flagship of the fleet, and the Olympics
item.description: Melbourne takes over as RAN flagship and spends her first year working.

item.title: The angled deck, as drawn in the sim
item.description: Why a carrier's landing area is angled away from the ship's axis, and how the sim lays it out.

item.title: 1956: sixty-four aircraft and a long way home
item.description: The maiden voyage from Scotland to Sydney with three squadrons embarked.

item.title: Seven cameras and when to use each
item.description: Orbit, Deck, Island, Approach, Flyby, Cockpit and Chase: what each camera is for.

item.title: 6 December 1955: the first aircraft lands
item.description: The first aircraft to touch down was a Royal Navy Westland Whirlwind helicopter.

item.title: What the model still gets wrong
item.description: An honest list of where the sim's ship is approximate, and why each item is on the list.

item.title: 28 October 1955: two names in two days
item.description: She was commissioned as HMAS Majestic and renamed Melbourne almost immediately.

item.title: The A-4G in the sim: livery and markings
item.description: What the reference photos show about the Skyhawk's paint and markings, and what the sim's aircraft currently wears.

item.title: Three inventions bolted onto a wartime hull
item.description: The angled deck, steam catapult and mirror landing sight changed carrier flying, and Melbourne got all three before she was finished.

item.title: Keyboard controls cheat sheet
item.description: Every key in the sim on one page: flight controls, cameras, and the commands for starting, stopping and restarting.

item.title: June 1947: Australia buys an unfinished carrier
item.description: How the RAN ended up with a half-built ship, a sister ship and a loan carrier.

item.title: Phase 2: a flyable A-4G Skyhawk
item.description: The ship got an aircraft: a Skyhawk with a simplified flight model, a cockpit view and a HUD, flown from the keyboard.
